_meta.note: Finalize the code-adapter branch as v1.25 (merge = the bump; proof-driven, no PR). Five items: (5) expose the now-Python-native adapters as MCP tools so an MCP client (Codex/Claude Code/OpenCode) gets node-free code-aware dep-lint + context in-session; (2) refresh docs/howto/build-a-domain-adapter.md — it predates the parity port and is node-only framing, must now say 'ship it in BOTH runtimes with a parity proof'; (3) refresh the README blurb (code + docs, both runtimes); (4) add the domain adapters to dev-plugin.md; (1) bump the version to v1.25 (plugin.json + marketplace.json 1.24.0->1.25.0; pyproject.toml 0.14.0->0.15.0; de-hardcode the T39.4 version test into a plugin==marketplace consistency check) and write the STATUS.md v1.25 changelog capturing the whole branch. Order MT->AR->VB so STATUS (VB, last) captures the MCP tools too. Spec-first; adversarial review each gate; keep node+python+parity+prose/self-audit green.

phases.title: Expose the adapters as MCP tools (node-free, in-session)

tasks.title: Author the MCP-adapters proof (spec-first)
tasks.description: Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/mcp-adapters.sh — drives the REAL `hb mcp-serve` stdio JSON-RPC server (like mcp-server.sh) using ONE server process, and asserts: (1) tools/list now includes `deplint` and `code_context`; (2) tools/call `deplint` with an inline {dag, codemap} (load plugin/adapters/code/fixtures/missing.dag.json + missing.codemap.json as the args) returns findings EQUAL to the Python adapter — the expected value is DERIVED in-process by importing `heartbeat.adapters.code.deplint.deplint(dag, codemap)` and comparing to the tool result (NOT a hardcoded literal), proving the tool calls the real library; (3) tools/call `code_context` with {codemap, task} (context.codemap.json, TA) returns text EQUAL to `heartbeat.adapters.code.codegraph_context.context_for(codemap, 'TA')`, again derived in-process. Print MCP-ADAPTERS-OK. Must fail before the tools are registered (tools/list lacks them / tools/call errors). Stdlib-only, no node; keep it under 5s (single server, no per-assertion CLI subprocess).

tasks.title: Register the deplint + code_context MCP tools
tasks.description: Add two tools to py/src/heartbeat/mcp_server.py TOOLS: `deplint` (args {dag: object, codemap: object} required) whose handler calls `from heartbeat.adapters.code.deplint import deplint as _dl; return _dl(a['dag'], a['codemap'])` returning {missing, redundant, collision}; and `code_context` (args {codemap: object, task: string} required) whose handler calls `from heartbeat.adapters.code.codegraph_context import context_for; return context_for(a['codemap'], a['task'])` returning the context string. Read-only (no state mutation), so they route like the read tools (tick/next/state) — they do NOT append events. Give each a clear description and JSON input schema. The MCP server stays stdlib-only; the tools reuse the parity-proven adapter functions (so an MCP client gets the capability with zero Node).

tasks.title: Wire the proof (T97) + document the new MCP tools
tasks.description: Add node-suite group T97 to tests/run-tests.sh, wired in the SINGLE-LINE form (so both the mtb regex `mcp-adapters.sh.*MCP-ADAPTERS-OK` AND self-audit are satisfied — do NOT use the two-line `bash x.sh > out` / `grep OK out` idiom): `check "T97.1 …" 'bash "$GEX/mcp-adapters.sh" 2>&1 | grep -q "MCP-ADAPTERS-OK"'`, guarded on python3. Update docs/howto/drive-heartbeat-over-mcp.md to list the new read tools (deplint, code_context) AND reference `gate-examples/mcp-adapters.sh` by name (so self-audit's referenced-proof integrity enforces its existence+wiring). Update docs/dev-python.md's MCP-server tool list to include deplint + code_context. Keep node+python+parity+prose/self-audit green.

phases.title: Refresh the adapter docs for the parity/both-runtimes reality

tasks.title: Add the both-runtimes/parity step to the recipe + README + dev-plugin
tasks.description: Update docs/howto/build-a-domain-adapter.md: it predates the parity port and is node-only framing. Add a step 'Ship it in both runtimes' — a domain adapter is a PARITY surface: implement it in BOTH node (plugin/adapters/<domain>/) and Python (py/src/heartbeat/adapters/<domain>/), cross-checked node == python by a parity proof (byte-equal for deterministic outputs, set-equal for maps), so the capability is native to the Python/framework path (node-free). Reference gate-examples/adapters-nodefree.sh. De-node-center the earlier steps (mention the python invocation alongside node). Update README.md: the adapters blurb should say the method is made 'code- and docs-aware' and that adapters ship in BOTH runtimes (node ≡ python). Update docs/dev-plugin.md: add a short entry pointing at the domain adapters (plugin/adapters/{code,docs}/), noting they are a parity surface with py/src/heartbeat/adapters/ (T94/T95) and not scaffolded into .hb. Keep every doc prose-clean (T79/T93) and self-audit green (links resolve, no fake hb commands).

phases.title: Bump to v1.25 + STATUS changelog (captures the whole branch)

tasks.title: Bump the version files + de-hardcode the version test + write STATUS v1.25
tasks.description: Bump the single-sourced version to v1.25: plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json and .claude-plugin/marketplace.json 1.24.0 -> 1.25.0; py/pyproject.toml 0.14.0 -> 0.15.0. De-hardcode the version test: change tests/run-tests.sh T39.4 (keep the check, do NOT delete it) from `grep 1.24.0 plugin.json` to a CONSISTENCY assertion — plugin.json's version === the marketplace.json heartbeat entry's version (derived, no literal) — so future bumps don't touch the test (and remove the stale '1.24.0' literal). Also refresh release/README.md: its 'New in v1.24' blurb must be updated to v1.25 (else the released note ships stale). Write the STATUS.md v1.25 section (update the top 'Version:' line to v1.25 and add a '## v1.25' entry) summarizing the ENTIRE branch since v1.24: viz --serve live dashboard (T86); the domain-adapter architecture (docs/adapters.md) with two shipped domains — code (CodeGraph) and docs/research (citation graph) — each Seam 1 (dep-lint) + Seam 2 (context hook); per-adapter skills + the skill-integrity gate (T92); whole-docs/ prose gating (T93); the T55.2 de-flake; the adapters PARITY PORT (node == python, T94/T95, node-free T96); and the MCP adapter tools (deplint + code_context, T97). Follow the repo's STATUS style (current-state, proof-referenced). Keep node+python+parity green (T39 now consistency-based).

GATE_MT.desc: The MCP server exposes `deplint` and `code_context` tools whose answers EQUAL the Python adapter functions (proven against the real mcp-serve JSON-RPC server), so an MCP client gets node-free code-aware dep-lint + context in-session; proof wired and the tools documented.

review.prompt: Refute that MT is done. Does mcp-adapters.sh drive the REAL mcp-serve server (JSON-RPC over stdio, not a stub) and assert tools/list includes deplint AND code_context AND that tools/call returns findings/text EQUAL to the Python adapter functions (heartbeat.adapters.code.deplint.deplint / codegraph_context.context_for) — so the tool calls the real library, not a reimplementation? Could MCP-ADAPTERS-OK print while a tool returns wrong/empty output (does it compare to the adapter's actual output, and does it FAIL before the tools are registered)? Are the tools READ-ONLY (no event appended, no state mutation)? Is the MCP server still stdlib-only? Are the tools actually documented (drive-heartbeat-over-mcp.md + dev-python.md), and is the proof wired (T97) and referenced by a how-to so self-audit enforces it?
